context.guidance: Do not write Personal Data or Authentication Secrets to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or outbound headers beyond what the session strictly needs. Keep identity in an opaque session identifier held server-side, and keep only non-Personal Data preferences in the browser. Where a value must be held client-side, protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires.

value.fix: Stop persisting the auth token in localStorage. Delete the `localStorage.setItem('token', authentication.token)` call and any reads of `localStorage.getItem('token')`. Have the server create an opaque, random session ID, store the identity and token server-side, and return only that ID in a `Set-Cookie` header with `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` and a bounded `Max-Age`. The browser then sends the cookie automatically, so client JavaScript never handles the token. If client code needs the token for API calls, keep it in memory only (never in localStorage, sessionStorage, or a cookie readable by JS), make it short-lived, and fetch it again from the server when needed. Do not put identity data or the token in other browser storage or outbound headers beyond what the request strictly requires. Keep only non-personal UI preferences client-side. On logout and on page load, clear any legacy `token` key from localStorage, and invalidate the server-side session. Verify by logging in and confirming that `localStorage` contains no `token` key, that the session cookie is HttpOnly and Secure, that authenticated requests succeed with the cookie alone, and that logout invalidates the session. Any client-side value that must remain must be protected as Rule 6(1)(a) requires, such as encryption at rest with a key the page cannot expose.
